submitter: bugs_open/440 lane, phase 1b — the first sanctioned producer of spec.routing_reason. Phase 1a (the inert livespec foundation, REB-008) was APPROVED r1 on correlation 55def842 and is shipped and ancestry-verified in build 7bf1ff674021. This round is the producer half: the item creator stamps the routing key alongside the existing reason. The gate still reads `reason` — the FLIP is RFC_062 phase 3 and is not in this submission. Owner ruled D1-D5 on 2026-09-03 (recorded in RFC_062 §Rulings); D5 lifted this lane's courtesy gate on the 404 lane, whose r4 is approved and who were told by CONTRIB before any edit to their file.
rationale: bugs_open/440: an unrecognised spec.reason routes to assemble and completes green, and refusal is impossible while one field carries both a routing key and free human prose. The split gives the routing half its own key. This round writes that key at the producer so that when RFC_062's phase-3 gate flips there is a populated key to flip TO, rather than a drain window in which every in-flight item routes to assemble. THE WHOLE CARE OF THIS CHANGE IS THE LOCKSTEP: RoutingKey is set exactly when KeyReason is, never on 'merely known'. image_landed WITHOUT a component_id deliberately stamps nothing — REB-001's designed degrade to assemble — so stamping a routing key there would make the phase-3 gate route a page that assembles today: a behaviour change disguised as a foundation, invisible until the flip made it production behaviour weeks later. Lockstep makes the flip provably byte-neutral for every reason that works correctly now. Second invariant: an unknown reason must leave the routing key EMPTY, enforced by control flow (the !known branch returns before the assignment) rather than by a check that could be edited away — otherwise phase 3's refusal would fire on items this very action minted, violating REB-008's no-bad-producer constraint at its own first producer. Third: the dedup key is untouched — pageRerenderItemKey still takes keyReason alone, so idx_swi_dedup behaviour cannot change, which is the one way an additive field could have altered live behaviour. All three are pinned by tests, and the two ways of getting the lockstep wrong are mutation-proved.

plan.summary: Two files. The creator gains a RoutingKey field on its pure decision struct, set in lockstep with KeyReason inside the existing StampReason guard, and writes spec[livespec.RoutingReasonSpecKey] beside spec["reason"] in the same guarded block. A new test file pins the lockstep across the whole (reason x component_id) matrix, the no-bad-key invariant using REAL observed unknowns, the producer/consumer round trip against livespec.ResolveRoutingReason, and the dedup key's independence from the addition.

edits.symbol: rerenderMode.RoutingKey, rerenderModeFor, the spec-building block in CreateRerenderItemsAction
edits.rationale: The field lives on the PURE struct the file already extracted for exhaustive DB-free testing, so the new invariant is testable by the real function rather than a re-implementation. It is assigned inside the existing StampReason guard (lockstep) and on the known-reason branch only (no bad key by control flow). The spec write sits in the same guarded block as spec["reason"], and the comment states that the dedup key deliberately does not include it.

The lockstep test sweeps the whole matrix (every vocabulary value x with/without component_id, plus empty and unknown) rather than a hand-picked example, so a future value cannot be silently exempt. The unknown test uses tool_retirement and light_palette_chrome_replaced — REAL observed unknowns from the census (16 and 13 live items), not synthetic strings. The round-trip test asserts producer and consumer agree via livespec.ResolveRoutingReason, the drift this vocabulary already suffered once. The dedup test proves the addition is inert for idx_swi_dedup.

grounded_in: The lockstep hazard, from the vocabulary's own definition [platform/livespec/rerender_reasons.go, RerenderSectionReasons]: image_landed and section_data_resolved are ComponentScoped WITHOUT StampAlways, and the file's own comment says why — 'DELIBERATELY NOT SET for image_landed and section_data_resolved. Those two carry REB-001's designed degrade — a reason without a component_id falls back to assemble-only — and preserving it byte-for-byte is not this bug's to change.' Stamping a routing key on merely-known would break exactly that at the flip.

The no-bad-key invariant is control flow, not a check [create_rerender_items_action.go, rerenderModeFor]: the !known branch sets m.UnknownReason, appends the warning and RETURNS before the assignment block is reached, so an out-of-vocabulary value has no path to the routing key.

The dedup key's shape [same file, pageRerenderItemKey -> discovery_checks.PageRerenderItemKey(pageName, siteID, keyReason)]: three arguments, keyReason among them, routing key absent — verified by reading the call site, and asserted by TestRoutingKeyIsNotPartOfTheDedupKey.

The real unknowns used as poison [live DB, 2026-09-02, bugs_open/440 census]: SELECT COALESCE(spec->>'reason','(none)'), count(*) FROM site_work_items WHERE item_type='page_rerender' GROUP BY 1 — tool_retirement 16 (2026-08-31), light_palette_chrome_replaced 13 (2026-08-25), both routing-shaped, both out-of-vocabulary, both silently assembled.

plan.risks: (1) The obvious risk is a behaviour change smuggled in as an additive field. Addressed structurally rather than by assertion: the routing key is written ONLY inside the block that already writes spec.reason, so any item that carries the new key already carried the old one; no gate reads the new key until phase 3; and the dedup key is proven unchanged. (2) The item spec grows one key for stamped items — cosmetic in a jsonb column, and it is the key phase 3 flips to; an item minted today therefore routes correctly after the flip instead of falling into the drain window. (3) SHARED FILE: three lanes have edited create_rerender_items_action.go in eight days (404's ef4236b4d, 384's 9a00a1ee9, 315-reopen's 8eca969cb on 2026-09-03). Read fresh at write time, committed by pathspec, and the diff is confined to the three hunks above (git diff --numstat: 32 insertions, 1 deletion). (4) REB-008 forbids a second producer of this key before RFC_062 lands — this action is the first and only one; the register entry is being updated in this commit to name it as such.
